question: An epidemic curve shows a single sharp peak with all cases clustered within one incubation period. This pattern is most consistent with which type of epidemic?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A propagated epidemic shows successive waves of cases over multiple incubation periods, not a single sharp peak.
Correct. A single sharp peak within one incubation period is the hallmark of a point-source common-source epidemic — all cases were exposed to the same source at approximately the same time.

answers.text: Mixed epidemic with both common and propagated spread

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A mixed epidemic shows an initial sharp peak followed by secondary waves. A single sharp peak indicates point-source exposure only.
Endemic patterns show baseline prevalence with seasonal variation, not the sharp single-peak pattern of a point-source epidemic.

overallFeedback.feedback: A single sharp peak within one incubation period indicates point-source common-source exposure — the hallmark of a common-source epidemic.
Correct! A single sharp peak within one incubation period is the classic pattern of a point-source common-source epidemic.
